construction_markdown:
### Outer field and curve

Let `p(X)=X^8+X^4+X^3+X+1` and `K=F_2[theta]/(p)=F_256`. Starting with `F_1=K(x_1)`, define

`F_{i+1}=F_i(z_{i+1})`, `z_{i+1}^16+z_{i+1}=x_i^17`, `x_{i+1}=z_{i+1}/x_i`.

For the top extension `F_5/F_4`, let `sigma_a(z_5)=z_5+a` for `a in F_16`, and take

`H=F_5^{<sigma_1>}=F_4(y)`, `y=z_5^2+z_5`,

so `y^8+y^4+y^2+y=x_4^17`. This field has exact genus `g=553,601` and exactly `L=8,356,224` rational places.

Order those places by the Garcia–Stichtenoth classes `A_4,C_4,S^(4)`, then by polynomial-basis residue data and exact local branch data. Select the first

`t=29,191`

places in the unramified split class `A_4` as jet places. At such a place `P`, use `u_P=x_1-x_1(P)` as uniformizer and write

`f=f_{P,0}+f_{P,1}u_P+O(u_P^2)`.

The other `L-t=8,327,033` places receive ordinary evaluations.

### Divisor and message space

Let `P_inf` be the unique place above the pole of `x_1`, and set

`a=1,041,734`, `A=65,466 P_inf`, `K_can=(dx_1)`, `E=K_can-A`.

Then `deg E=a`. The functions `1,x_1,z_2` have distinct sole-pole orders `0,32,768,34,816`, so `ell(A)>=3`. Move `E` by weak approximation to a linearly equivalent divisor `G` whose coefficient at every evaluation place is zero. Riemann–Roch gives

`ell(G)>=a+1-g+ell(A)>=488,137`.

Choose the first `488,137` independent functions in the deterministic height ordering and let their `K`-span be `V`.

### Ordinary inner flag

Over `F_2[beta]/(beta^7+beta+1)`, let `A_15` be the parity extension of the length-127 BCH code with roots `beta^1,...,beta^54`, and let `A_8` be the parity extension of the code with roots `beta^1,...,beta^62`. Then

`A_8=[128,8,>=64]_2` is contained in `A_15=[128,15,>=56]_2`.

Fix an isomorphism `K -> A_8` and choose the first two independent quotient representatives `r_1,r_2` of `A_15/A_8`.

### Jet Construction-X flag

Use an independent auxiliary field

`B=F_2[alpha]/(alpha^8+alpha^4+alpha^3+alpha^2+1)`,

where `alpha` is primitive. Let `B_119` and `B_111` be the binary length-255 BCH codes with roots respectively `alpha^1,...,alpha^118` and `alpha^1,...,alpha^110`. Extend each by its parity coordinate:

`C_13=ext(B_119)=[256,13,>=120]_2`,

`E_21=ext(B_111)=[256,21,>=112]_2`,

with `C_13 subset E_21`. Extend the standard basis of `C_13` deterministically to a basis of `E_21`; call the first five quotient representatives `q_1,...,q_5`.

Let `S_7=[7,3,4]_2` be the simplex code obtained by evaluating linear forms on the seven nonzero vectors of `F_2^3`, in binary-integer order. Put

`S_3={(s,s):s in S_7}=[14,3,8]_2`.

Pair `q_1,q_2,q_3` with a fixed basis of `S_3`. The resulting graph code

`J_16 subset F_2^{256+14}`

has parameters `[270,16,>=120]_2`: the zero quotient uses `C_13`, while every nonzero quotient has main weight at least 112 and tail weight 8.

For the two top directions, pair `q_4,q_5` with

`a_0=(1^7,0^7)=0x007f`, `b_0=(v,v)=0x0387`,

where `v` indicates the first three simplex coordinates `001,010,011`. Modulo `S_3`, the three nonzero cosets represented by `a_0,b_0,a_0+b_0` have respective distances `7,6,7`.

### Encoder

The message is `(f,tau) in V x F_2^2`. At an ordinary place encode `f(P)` in `A_8` and add `tau_1 r_1+tau_2 r_2`.

At jet place `P_j`, map `(f_{P_j,0},f_{P_j,1}) in K^2` through the fixed bit-basis isomorphism onto `J_16`. Let

`M=[[0,1],[1,1]] in GL(2,2)`.

If `M^j tau=(e_1,e_2)`, add the 270-bit vector

`e_1(q_4,a_0)+e_2(q_5,b_0)`.

Finally append 30 zero coordinates. Every basis, complement, isomorphism, local parameter, place order, and divisor translate is selected by the stated polynomial-basis, row-reduction, and height-first conventions; there is no random choice.
distance_audit: For `tau=0`, let `o` be the number of zero ordinary evaluations and `j` the number of jet places where both local coefficients vanish. Divisor degree gives `o+2j<=a`.
Every nonzero ordinary bottom block has weight at least 64 and every nonzero jet bottom block has weight at least 120. Hence `wt>=64(L-t-o)+120(t-j)>=64(L-a)+56t=469,762,056`.
For `tau!=0`, every ordinary block lies in a nonzero `A_15/A_8` coset and therefore has weight at least 56.
At every jet place the main component lies in a nonzero `E_21/C_13` quotient direction and contributes at least 112. The three auxiliary quotient separations are `7,6,7`.

Since `29,191=3*9,730+1`, cycling the three nonzero labels gives every nonzero top message auxiliary weight at least `20*9,730+6=194,606`. Thus its total weight is at least `56(L-t)+112t+194,606=469,777,846`.
The certified minimum-distance lower bound is therefore `min(469,762,056,469,777,846)=469,762,056`, eight above the campaign target.
explicitness_audit: The outer constant field is fixed by a displayed irreducible polynomial and ordered polynomial basis.
Every tower field, intermediate subgroup, and defining equation is displayed. The exact rational places are classified and deterministically ordered.
Jet places are the first 29,191 places in a specified split class; their uniformizers are explicitly `x_1-x_1(P)`.
The divisor translate is the first exact weak-approximation solution in a finite-shell enumeration. The selected Riemann–Roch subspace has exactly 488,137 `K`-dimensions.
All four cyclic constituents are defined by displayed consecutive root sets over displayed primitive-field presentations. Complements are selected by canonical row reduction.
The repeated simplex tail, its two quotient vectors, the order-three balancing matrix, coordinate orders, and 30 right-padding coordinates are explicit.
All searches and enumerations use exact finite-field or divisor arithmetic. No random sampling, probabilistic existence claim, or hidden asymptotic constant occurs.

obstructions: The rate does not cross `7/1920`. The strict integer threshold is dimension `3,914,684`, so this construction remains 9,586 dimensions short.

With the present top two bits, crossing by Riemann–Roch alone would require `488,137+1,199=489,336` outer dimensions. Since the current formula is `488,134+ell(65,466P_inf)`, this would require `ell(65,466P_inf)>=1,202`; only three independent functions are presently certified. Equality at three is not proved.

The 14-coordinate bottom tail is Griesmer-minimal for a `[14,3,8]` code. Within this displayed Construction-X flag, an exact finite coset computation also blocks a third balanced top bit; this is a local obstruction, not a universal impossibility theorem.

The mechanism genuinely leaves the vanilla one-symbol GS/RM template by using multiplicity-two evaluations and a heterogeneous Construction-X flag, but its proved finite rate still lies below that template's asymptotic envelope.

proof_markdown:
### Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code

`C subset F_2^1,073,741,824`

with dimension `3,905,098` and minimum distance at least `469,762,056`.

### 1. Exact outer function field

For `p(X)=X^8+X^4+X^3+X+1`, direct reduction gives `X^256=X mod p` and `gcd(p,X^16+X)=1`; Rabin's criterion proves that `p` is irreducible. Every tower equation has derivative one in its newly adjoined variable, so the tower is separable.

The full-level genus formula gives

`g(F_4)=67,185`, `g(F_5)=1,109,505`.

Consequently

`deg Diff(F_5/F_4)=(2g(F_5)-2)-16(2g(F_4)-2)=69,120`.

For `c in F_16^*`, the scaling `x_i -> c x_i`, `z_i -> c^2 z_i` preserves the tower and conjugates the fifteen nonidentity translations transitively. Hilbert's different formula therefore assigns each nonidentity translation contribution `69,120/15=4,608`. Since `F_5/H` is the degree-two extension generated by `sigma_1`,

`deg Diff(F_5/H)=4,608`.

Hurwitz now gives

`2,219,008=2(2g(H)-2)+4,608`,

hence `g(H)=553,601`.

At level `F_4`, the exact rational-place classes have sizes

`|A_4|=(256-1)16^3=1,044,480`, `|C_4|=16`, `|S^(4)|=256`.

The first two classes split completely and the last is totally ramified. Thus

`N_1(H)=8(1,044,480+16)+256=8,356,224=L`.

### 2. The divisor space

The infinite place is totally ramified. Since `[H:F_1]=32,768`, `x_1` has sole-pole order `32,768`. In the second tower field, `z_2` has pole order 17, and `[H:F_2]=2,048`; hence its pullback has sole-pole order `34,816`. Therefore `1,x_1,z_2` are independent elements of `L(65,466P_inf)` and

`ell(65,466P_inf)>=3`.

Let `K_can=(dx_1)`, `A=65,466P_inf`, and `E=K_can-A`. Since `2g-2=1,107,200`,

`deg E=1,107,200-65,466=1,041,734=a`.

For every evaluation place `P`, weak approximation supplies a principal translate `G=E+(h)` with `v_P(G)=0`. The prescribed height-first enumeration makes the choice of `h` deterministic. Since `K_can-G` is linearly equivalent to `A`, Riemann–Roch yields

`ell(G)=a+1-g+ell(K_can-G)`

`>=1,041,735-553,601+3=488,137`.

Choose a `K`-linear subspace `V subset L(G)` of exactly that dimension. All its functions are regular at every evaluation place.

### 3. Inner-code parameters

For length 127, the binary cyclotomic cosets meeting exponents `1,...,54` have total degree 112; adjoining the coset first met at exponent 55 raises the degree to 119 for exponents `1,...,62`. The BCH bound and parity extension therefore give a nested flag

`A_8=[128,8,>=64]_2 subset A_15=[128,15,>=56]_2`.

For length 255, the unions of binary cyclotomic cosets meeting `1,...,110` and `1,...,118` have sizes 234 and 242. Thus the corresponding cyclic codes have dimensions 21 and 13 and designed distances 111 and 119. Extending by parity makes every weight even, giving

`C_13=[256,13,>=120]_2 subset E_21=[256,21,>=112]_2`.

Choose quotient representatives `q_1,...,q_5` independent modulo `C_13`. Let `S_7` be the `[7,3,4]` simplex code and `S_3={(s,s):s in S_7}`. Pairing `q_1,q_2,q_3` with a basis of `S_3` gives a 16-dimensional graph code `J_16`. If the quotient label is zero, a nonzero graph word lies in `C_13` and has weight at least 120. If the quotient label is nonzero, its 256-coordinate component is a nonzero word of `E_21` and its 14-coordinate component is a nonzero word of `S_3`; its weight is at least `112+8=120`. Hence

`J_16=[270,16,>=120]_2`.

For the top quotient, let `v` indicate the Fano line `{001,010,011}`. Direct evaluation of the eight simplex words shows that `wt(v+s)` is 3 for seven choices of `s in S_7` and 7 for the remaining choice. With

`a_0=(1^7,0^7)`, `b_0=(v,v)`,

we obtain

`d(a_0,S_3)=7`, `d(b_0,S_3)=6`, `d(a_0+b_0,S_3)=7`.

Indeed, words in the first and third cosets have the form `(w,1+w)` up to swapping, and hence have constant weight seven; the second coset has weights twice those of `v+S_7`.

### 4. Linearity, length, and dimension

All evaluation, local-expansion, inner-encoding, quotient-section, and balancing maps are `F_2`-linear, so the image is a binary linear code.

The exact unpadded length is

`128(L-t)+270t=128L+142t=1,073,741,794`.

Appending 30 zeros gives `n=2^30`.

To prove injectivity, first suppose the encoded word is zero. A nonzero top message has a nonzero `A_15/A_8` label at every ordinary place, so the top message must be zero. The remaining zero word implies that `f` vanishes at every ordinary place and to order at least two at every jet place. Its certified zero divisor then has degree at least

`(L-t)+2t=L+t=8,385,415>a`,

which is impossible for nonzero `f in L(G)`. Thus `f=0`. The dimension is therefore

`8 dim_K(V)+2=8*488,137+2=3,905,098`.

### 5. Distance when the top message is zero

Let `o` count ordinary places where `f(P)=0`, and let `j` count jet places where both local coefficients vanish. Since `G` has coefficient zero at these places,

`(f)+G-Z>=0`, `deg Z>=o+2j`,

so `o+2j<=a` for nonzero `f`.

Every remaining ordinary block has weight at least 64 and every remaining jet block has weight at least 120. Therefore

`wt>=64(L-t-o)+120(t-j)`

`=64(L-t)+120t-(64o+120j)`

`>=64(L-t)+120t-64a`

`=64(L-a)+56t`

`=468,127,360+1,634,696`

`=469,762,056`.

The inequality uses `64o+120j<=64(o+2j)`.

### 6. Distance when the top message is nonzero

At every ordinary place, the word lies in a nonzero coset of `A_8` inside `A_15`, so it has weight at least 56.

At jet place `P_j`, the two quotient directions are permuted by `M^j`. Since `M` has order three, each nonzero top message encounters the three nonzero labels once per three consecutive jet places. The 256-coordinate main component is always nonzero modulo the bottom graph and contributes at least 112. The auxiliary separations are `7,6,7`.

Because `t=3*9,730+1`, the total auxiliary contribution for every nonzero top message is at least

`20*9,730+6=194,606`.

Hence

`wt>=56(L-t)+112t+194,606`

`=466,313,848+3,269,392+194,606`

`=469,777,846`.

Combining the two cases proves `d_min(C)>=469,762,056`.

### 7. Rate and ceiling comparison

The exact rate is

`R=3,905,098/1,073,741,824=1,952,549/536,870,912`

`≈0.003636905923485756`.

This improves the verified dimension `3,688,448` by `216,650`. However,

`7/1920-R=71,893/8,053,063,680>0`.

Thus the construction does not beat the ceiling. Its multiplicity-two evaluations and heterogeneous Construction-X flag genuinely leave the vanilla one-level GS/RM parameter formula, but the proved finite rate remains below `7/1920`.

proof_steps.proof: Rabin's criterion verifies the displayed degree-eight field. The recursive equations are separable, and the fixed-field equation follows from `y=z_5^2+z_5`.
proof_steps.statement: The outer field, tower, and intermediate field are deterministic and well-defined.

proof_steps.proof: The full-step different has degree 69,120. Scaling conjugates all fifteen nonidentity translations, so each contributes 4,608. Hurwitz for `F_5/H` gives genus 553,601. Exact split and ramified classes give 8,356,224 rational places.
proof_steps.statement: The intermediate field has exact genus 553,601 and exactly 8,356,224 rational places.

proof_steps.proof: The three displayed functions certify `ell(65,466P_inf)>=3`. Moving `K_can-65,466P_inf` off all evaluation places and applying Riemann–Roch gives at least 488,137 independent `K`-messages.
proof_steps.statement: There is a deterministic admissible divisor `G` of degree 1,041,734 and an exact 488,137-dimensional selected message space.

proof_steps.proof: Cyclotomic-coset counts give the exact constituent dimensions; parity extension changes the odd designed-distance bounds 63,55,119,111 to even lower bounds 64,56,120,112.
proof_steps.statement: The ordinary nested BCH flag has parameters `[128,8,64] subset [128,15,56]`, and the jet main flag has `[256,13,120] subset [256,21,112]`.

proof_steps.proof: The repeated simplex has parameters `[14,3,8]`. The graph construction gives `[270,16,120]`. Direct Fano-line weight calculation gives quotient separations 7,6,7 for the two top directions.
proof_steps.statement: The jet Construction-X flag and its two top quotient directions have the claimed weights.

proof_steps.proof: The encoder is binary linear. Its raw length is 1,073,741,794 and it receives 30 fixed zeros. Injectivity follows from the ordinary quotient when the top message is nonzero and from `L+t>a` when it is zero.
proof_steps.statement: The final code has exact length 1,073,741,824 and exact dimension 3,905,098.

proof_steps.proof: For zero top message, `o+2j<=a` and block weights give 469,762,056. For nonzero top message, the order-three quotient cycle gives 469,777,846. The smaller bound is the certified minimum distance.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonzero codeword has weight at least 469,762,056.

proof_steps.proof: Exact fraction arithmetic gives the displayed rate, its 216,650-dimension improvement over the verified record, and its positive gap below `7/1920`.
proof_steps.statement: This is a new leaderboard candidate but not a beyond-ceiling result.

research_direction: Multiplicity-two Garcia–Stichtenoth evaluation with a nested-BCH Construction-X inner code and a balanced two-bit generalized-concatenation layer.
theorem_statement: There exists a deterministic explicit binary linear code `[1,073,741,824,3,905,098,>=469,762,056]_2`. It improves the current verified dimension by 216,650 but remains below rate `7/1920`.
